mcqs.q: An impression is a ___ likeness and a cast is a ___ likeness.
mcqs.explain: The impression is the negative imprint; the cast poured into it is the positive reproduction.

mcqs.q: Which is an ideal requisite of an impression material?
opts: It should set without distorting or tearing on removal and stay dimensionally stable until poured
It should be toxic to inhibit bacteria
It should expand greatly on setting
mcqs.explain: Ideal materials adapt yet stay in the tray, set in reasonable time, resist distortion/tearing, remain dimensionally stable, are cost-effective and biocompatible.

mcqs.q: Which group of impression materials is RIGID (inelastic)?
opts: Impression plaster, compound, wax and ZOE
mcqs.explain: Rigid: plaster, compound, wax, ZOE. Elastic: hydrocolloids (alginate/agar) and elastomers.

mcqs.q: A material that sets by a reversible PHYSICAL reaction is termed:
mcqs.explain: Reversible/physical set = thermoplastic (e.g. compound, wax); irreversible/chemical = thermoset (e.g. plaster, ZOE, alginate).

mcqs.q: Impression plaster is essentially:
opts: Type-1 gypsum (calcium sulfate hemihydrate) with modifiers
mcqs.explain: Impression plaster is modified type-1 gypsum; hemihydrate + water → dihydrate on setting.

mcqs.q: Why can impression plaster NOT record undercuts?
opts: It is rigid/inelastic and would break
It is too viscous to reach them
mcqs.explain: Being rigid and non-elastic, plaster fractures if withdrawn over an undercut.

mcqs.q: Two properties that make plaster less suitable as an impression material are:
opts: Prolonged setting time (~15 min) and setting expansion
mcqs.explain: Its long set (~15 min) and setting expansion are drawbacks (expansion controlled with an anti-expansion solution).

mcqs.q: Impression waxes (e.g. Iowa/Korecta wax) are chiefly used to:
opts: Correct small imperfections and border extension of an impression
Take a full primary edentulous impression alone
Record deep undercuts on natural teeth
Serve as a permanent denture base
mcqs.explain: Corrective waxes fill defects, correct borders and register soft-tissue detail as a veneer over an impression.

mcqs.q: Impression compound (ADA No. 3) sets by:
opts: A reversible physical process — used warm (~45°C) then cooled to a rigid mass
mcqs.explain: Compound is thermoplastic: softened by heat (~45°C) and rigid when cooled to mouth temperature.

mcqs.q: In low-fusing (Type I) impression compound, the STICK form is mainly used for:
opts: Border molding of a custom tray
The full edentulous impression in a stock tray
mcqs.explain: Type I cakes take edentulous impressions; sticks are used for border molding/peripheral tracing.

mcqs.q: Prolonged immersion of impression compound in the water bath makes it:
mcqs.explain: Over-immersion leaches components, leaving the compound brittle and grainy. Loses low-molecular-weight components.

mcqs.q: Which is a disadvantage of impression compound?
opts: It does not reproduce fine surface detail and cannot record undercuts
It is too elastic for edentulous ridges
It sets instantly and cannot be re-adapted
mcqs.explain: Compound gives poor fine detail, distorts, and cannot handle undercuts; but it is non-toxic and re-adaptable.

mcqs.q: Zinc-oxide eugenol impression paste (ADA No. 16) is supplied as:
opts: A two-paste system (base with zinc oxide, catalyst with eugenol) that forms a chelate
A single powder mixed with water
mcqs.explain: The base (ZnO + vegetable oil) reacts with the catalyst (eugenol + rosin/fillers) to form a zinc-eugenolate chelate.

mcqs.q: For a ZOE impression, the impression should be SEATED in the mouth before the:
mcqs.explain: Seat before the initial set (3–6 min); withdraw only after the final set (10–15 min).

mcqs.q: A recognized USE of ZOE impression paste is:
opts: Final impressions of edentulous ridges with minor or no undercuts
Impressions of teeth with deep undercuts
Making diagnostic casts of dentate arches
As a permanent luting cement for crowns
mcqs.explain: ZOE is used for final edentulous impressions (no undercuts), wash impressions, temporary relines and perio packs.

mcqs.q: A disadvantage of ZOE impression paste is that:
opts: The eugenol can cause a burning sensation and tissue irritation
It cannot record any surface detail
It sets far too quickly to use
mcqs.explain: ZOE gives excellent detail and is stable, but it is sticky and its eugenol can irritate/burn tissues.

mcqs.q: Impression materials are used for the reproduction of:
opts: Hard and soft tissues of the mouth
The occlusal surfaces of teeth only
mcqs.explain: They allow casts — reproductions of the teeth and ridges made from gypsum products — to be created.

mcqs.q: A cast made for fabricating a definitive removable or fixed prosthesis is called a:
mcqs.explain: Diagnostic (preliminary) casts are used for diagnosis and treatment planning.

mcqs.q: Which is an ideal requisite concerning dimensional stability?
opts: The material must remain dimensionally stable at least until the cast is poured
The material must remain stable indefinitely after setting
The material must expand slightly on setting
The material must contract on setting to aid removal
mcqs.explain: Stability only has to last until pouring, which is why prompt pouring is emphasised.

mcqs.q: Which is listed among the ideal requisites of an impression material?
opts: It should set only on heating
It should bond chemically to enamel
mcqs.explain: Cost-effectiveness of the material, equipment and processing time is another requisite.

mcqs.q: The ELASTIC impression materials comprise:
opts: The hydrocolloids and the non-aqueous elastomers
Impression compound and zinc oxide eugenol
mcqs.explain: Rigid materials are impression plaster, wax, compound and zinc oxide eugenol.

mcqs.q: The main component of impression plaster is calcium sulphate hemihydrate, which reacts with water to form:
mcqs.explain: Impression plaster is dental plaster (type 1 gypsum) to which modifiers have been added.

mcqs.q: Raw plaster is unsuitable as an impression material because of:
opts: A prolonged setting time of about 15 minutes and setting expansion
A very short setting time and setting contraction
Its elasticity and poor detail reproduction
Its high viscosity and exothermic set
mcqs.explain: Modifiers are added to overcome these two properties.

mcqs.q: When mixing impression plaster, the powder is sprinkled into water and left for about:
mcqs.explain: It is then mixed to a homogeneous consistency.

mcqs.q: A specific indication for impression plaster is an impression of:
opts: Patients with excessively mobile soft tissues over the residual ridges
mcqs.explain: Its very low viscosity records mobile tissue without displacing it; it cannot record undercuts without breaking.

mcqs.q: Which is a DISADVANTAGE of impression plaster?
opts: It requires a separator before pouring, which leads to surface inaccuracy
Its rate of set cannot be controlled
It is incompatible with cast materials
mcqs.explain: Other disadvantages are that it cannot be added to, washes away in very wet mouths, induces nausea, and its exothermic heat is disliked.

mcqs.q: Impression waxes are composed of paraffin wax, bees wax, ceresin and:
opts: Metal particles such as aluminium or copper
mcqs.explain: They are available as Iowa Wax and Korecta Wax, graded No.1 extra-hard to No.4 extra-soft.

mcqs.q: A corrective impression wax is:
opts: A wax veneer placed over the original impression to register soft-tissue detail
A wax used to make the custom tray
A wax used to block out undercuts on the cast
A wax used to seal the posterior palatal seal
mcqs.explain: Waxes are also applied in small quantities to fill defects and correct border extension.

mcqs.q: Why can impression waxes NOT be stored?
opts: They distort from the release of internal stress
They react with the cast material
mcqs.explain: They are also technique sensitive and record edentulous surfaces only.

mcqs.q: Which colour of impression compound stick has the HIGHEST softening temperature?
opts: All three soften at the same temperature
mcqs.explain: Green is the lowest and gray is intermediate.

mcqs.q: The largest single ingredient group in impression compound is:
opts: Rosin and copal rosin — 30 parts each
mcqs.explain: Together the two rosins make up 60 of the 100 parts.

mcqs.q: Impression compound is used warm at about 45 °C and becomes rigid at:
mcqs.explain: This is a reversible physical (thermoplastic) process, not a chemical one.

mcqs.q: Impression compound and ZOE are both disinfected by:
opts: Immersion in 2% glutaraldehyde or an iodophor solution for 10 minutes
Spraying only, because they distort on immersion
Immersion in sodium hypochlorite for 30 minutes
mcqs.explain: Alginate, by contrast, must be sprayed because it distorts on immersion.

mcqs.q: In ZOE impression paste, the base paste consists of:
mcqs.explain: The catalyst paste is eugenol 12%, rosin 50%, fillers 20%, lanolin 3%, balsam 10% and accelerators 5%; the two react to form a chelate.

mcqs.q: The ADA initial and final setting times for ZOE impression paste are:
mcqs.explain: The impression must be seated before the initial set and may be withdrawn after the final set.

mcqs.q: Which is a recognised USE of ZOE paste apart from impressions?
opts: A surgical pack in periodontal surgery
A luting cement for metal crowns
A die material for fixed prosthodontics
A border-moulding material for stock trays
mcqs.explain: Temporary denture relines and wash impressions with compound are its other uses.

saqs.q: List four ideal requisites of an impression material.
saqs.a: Fluid enough to adapt to the oral tissues; viscous enough to be contained in the tray; sets to a rubbery or rigid solid in a reasonable time; does not distort or tear on removal; dimensionally stable at least until the cast is poured; cost-effective; and biocompatible.

list: Fluid enough to adapt to the oral tissues
Viscous enough to be contained in the tray
Sets to a rubbery or rigid solid in a reasonable time
Does not distort or tear on removal
Dimensionally stable at least until the cast is poured

saqs.q: Classify impression materials by elasticity and by setting mechanism, with an example of each.
saqs.a: BY ELASTICITY — rigid/inelastic: impression plaster, compound, wax, ZOE; elastic: hydrocolloids (alginate, agar) and elastomers (polysulfide, polyether, silicones). BY SETTING — irreversible/chemical (thermoset): plaster, ZOE, alginate; reversible/physical (thermoplastic): impression compound, wax, agar.

saqs.q: Describe impression plaster: its nature, why it cannot record undercuts, and two disadvantages.
saqs.a: Impression plaster is modified TYPE-1 GYPSUM (calcium sulfate hemihydrate) — irreversible, non-elastic and low-viscosity; hemihydrate + water → dihydrate on setting. It CANNOT record undercuts because, being rigid, it breaks on withdrawal. DISADVANTAGES — prolonged setting (~15 min) with setting expansion; washed away in wet mouths; exothermic heat and nausea; needs a separator, giving surface inaccuracy.

rows: modified type-1 gypsum (calcium sulfate hemihydrate) — irreversible, non-elastic, low-viscosity; hemihydrate + water → dihydrate on setting

list: Washed away in wet mouths, spoiling detail

saqs.q: Describe impression compound (Type I vs Type II) and its setting behaviour.
saqs.a: Compound (ADA No. 3) is REVERSIBLE, non-elastic and high-viscosity, and cannot record undercuts. TYPE I (lower fusing) — cakes for edentulous impressions and sticks, colour-coded by softening temperature, for border molding. TYPE II (higher fusing) — tray-adaptation material for a primary impression that then supports a thin second material. SETTING is a REVERSIBLE PHYSICAL change — softened warm (~45 °C) in a thermostatic water bath, rigid when cooled to 37 °C.

ans.text: ADA No. 3 — reversible, non-elastic, high-viscosity; it cannot record undercuts.

saqs.q: For ZOE impression paste, give its composition (base and catalyst) and its two setting times.
saqs.a: BASE PASTE — zinc oxide (~87%) + vegetable oil. CATALYST PASTE — eugenol (oil of cloves) + polymerized rosin + fillers + lanolin + resinous balsam + accelerators. They react to form a CHELATE. SETTING TIMES — initial 3–6 minutes (seat before the initial set) and final 10–15 minutes (withdraw at the final set).

saqs.q: Give the uses, advantages and disadvantages of impression plaster.
saqs.a: USES — impressions of edentulous ridges; of patients with excessively mobile soft tissue over the ridges; and of the mouth and face. ADVANTAGES — good surface detail; dimensionally accurate with an anti-expansion solution; rate of set under operator control; compatible with all cast materials; economical. DISADVANTAGES — cannot be added to if faulty; washes away in very wet mouths, especially lower impressions; induces nausea from its taste and rough feel; exothermic heat disliked by patients; requires a separator, leading to surface inaccuracy.

saqs.q: Describe impression waxes — their nature, composition, forms and uses.
saqs.a: Impression waxes are REVERSIBLE and NON-ELASTIC, used to correct small imperfections in impressions; they flow readily at mouth temperature and are relatively soft even at room temperature. COMPOSITION — paraffin wax, bees wax, ceresin and metal particles (aluminium or copper). FORMS — Iowa Wax and Korecta Wax, graded No.1 extra-hard to No.4 extra-soft. USES — filling defects and correcting border extension, and as a corrective wax veneer over the original impression to register soft-tissue detail. ADVANTAGES — easy to manipulate, no advanced equipment, thin accurate layers, odourless, no tissue reaction, economical. DISADVANTAGES — technique sensitive; cannot be stored, as stress release distorts it; records edentulous surfaces only.
